text.p: The following are leading domestic stories in Portuguese newspapers.
- Portuguese companies heavily indebted to social security system, a government source told the paper.
- Budget for education to rise more than seven percent in 1997, an official source told the paper.
- The jury presiding over the privatisation of tobacco company Tabaqueira should conclude its report next week, a member of the jury told the paper.
- Portugal's cable TV network TC Cabo is studying the possibility of lowering its installation prices, its president Graca Bau told the paper.

- The government should earn around 450 billion escudos from the privatisations of stakes in EDP-Electricidade de Portugal, airport company ANA and pulp group Portucel Industrial in 1997, Under-Secretary for Finance, Fernando Teixeira dos Santos, told the paper.
- The European Commission says Portugal must reduce its sardine fishing fleet but by less than previously recommended.

- Economy Minister Augusto Mateus prepares a plan to support operations of Portuguese companies abroad. The plan due to be launched in November should incorporate state financing of 50 billion escudos.
- Portuguese businessman Antonio Champalimaud, whose group controls Banco Pinto & Sotto Maior and Banco Totta & Azores, said the two would retain separate identities in a group reorganisation.
